drafts.email1:
Hi Kimberly,

I came across NCT06736418, your Phase 1a/1b study of 225Ac-ABD147 in SCLC and LCNEC.

Phase 1 oncology programs like this one are where the PK characterization and dose-escalation design shape everything downstream. For a novel agent like 225Ac-ABD147, getting the exposure-safety relationship characterized now also strengthens the IND safety updates and sets up a much cleaner Phase 2 transition. Furthermore, a limited patient enrollment (<20) would require the application of Bayesian and ML approaches for extracting maximum information from the sparse data.

Our team at PumasAI includes pharmacometricians and clinical pharmacologists, several having previous experiences from FDA, Novartis, and BMS. We've supported 75+ regulatory submissions across FDA, EMA, PMDA, NMPA, TGA, and CDSCO, with 37 Phase 3 programs delivered to date. We handle the full clinical pharmacology program end-to-end: NCA, PopPK, dose-escalation modeling, PK/PD characterization, and regulatory writing through submission.

Would a short call make sense to see if there's a fit?
drafts.subject2: Re: NCT07052760: Early-Phase PK & Dose Characterization
drafts.fu1:
Hi Kimberly,

Wanted to follow up briefly on my earlier note about NCT07052760.

One thing we hear consistently from early-phase oncology teams: PK data interpretation becomes a bottleneck right when dose-escalation decisions are time-sensitive. Our modeling platform (Pumas) runs these analyses 10x faster than traditional tools like NONMEM, which translates directly into faster dose decisions.

We recently supported a Phase 1 FIH program where our NCA + PopPK package directly informed the dose-escalation committee, getting to RP2D two months ahead of the original timeline. Would it be worth 15 minutes to see if the timing works for Abdera Therapeutics Inc.?
